tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate MD__New folder_SM -Calcium Carbonate MD.txt:30

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg sample in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; stepwise add 0.9 mL, 2 mL, 7 mL solvent (same shake and hold) to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble) then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble.

details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters; USP Description and Relative Solubility

tests.source: Calcium Carbonate MD__New folder_SM -Calcium Carbonate MD.txt:31

tests.procedure: Carbonates: suspend 0.1 g of the substance in 2 mL of water, add 3 mL of 2 M acetic acid; the solution or suspension effervesces, evolving a colourless and odourless gas. (Test 1, first step, as written: addition of acetic acid to 0.1 g produces effervescence.)

details.reference: USP Identification Tests-General, Calcium <191>; BP Appendix VI (Carbonates)

tests.source: Calcium Carbonate MD__New folder_SM -Calcium Carbonate MD.txt:32

tests.procedure: Calcium: dissolve about 20 mg of the substance (as written: 0.2 mL of solution S) in 5 mL of acetic acid; add 0.5 mL potassium ferrocyanide solution, the solution remains clear; add about 50 mg ammonium chloride; a white crystalline precipitate is formed.

details.reagent: 0.5 mL potassium ferrocyanide solution (5.3 g in water to 100 mL)

tests.source: Calcium Carbonate MD__New folder_SM -Calcium Carbonate MD.txt:32

tests.procedure: Acid-insoluble substances: mix 5.0 g sample with 10 mL water; add hydrochloric acid dropwise with agitation until effervescence ceases; add water to 200 mL and filter; wash the residue with water until the last washing shows no chloride; ignite; weigh the residue.
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate MD__New folder_SM -Calcium Carbonate MD.txt:33

tests.procedure: Heavy metals limit test: test solution 1.0 g dissolved in 5 mL dilute acetic acid, diluted to 12 mL with water, 2 mL pH 3.5 buffer added. Standard: 1 mL of 20 ppm lead, 2 mL pH 3.5 buffer, 1.2 mL thioacetamide reagent (mixed immediately). Examine after 2 min; any brown colour in the test solution is not more intense than the reference.
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate MD__New folder_SM -Calcium Carbonate MD.txt:34

tests.procedure: Weigh accurately an empty weighing bottle previously dried at 200 ± 10 °C and cooled in desiccator (W0); weigh 1.000 g sample into it (W1); dry in calibrated oven at 200 ± 10 °C for 4 h, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2); repeat to constant weight. % Loss on drying = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

details.reference: BP Appendix IX D; USP Loss on Drying <731>

tests.source: Calcium Carbonate MD__New folder_SM -Calcium Carbonate MD.txt:35

tests.procedure: Tapped density: weigh a 10 mL empty, dry cylinder and set as zero; pour the sample into the cylinder to the volume; record the weight of sample. Tapped density = Wt / Vol (g/mL).
tests.source: Calcium Carbonate MD__New folder_SM -Calcium Carbonate MD.txt:36

tests.procedure: Assay (complexometric titration): dissolve 0.150 g sample in 3 mL dilute hydrochloric acid and 20 mL water; boil 2 min, cool, dilute to 50 mL with water; add 6.0 mL strong sodium hydroxide solution and about 200 mg calconcarboxylic acid triturate; titrate with 0.1 M sodium edetate from violet to full blue. 1 mL of 0.1 M sodium edetate = 4.008 mg Ca. Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt.

details.equivalenceFactor: 1 mL of 0.1 M sodium edetate = 4.008 mg Ca
details.formula: Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt; E.P = end point titre; eq.wt = equivalent weight of Ca; F = titrant factor; Wt = sample weight (mg)
